A character model sheet for a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, the house look, as the reference image shows it. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. This is a model sheet for the animators, not a scene: a plain warm cream paper ground with a soft paper grain and no place behind, one thin flat ground line in a slightly deeper cream under the figures that stand, and a small soft violet contact shadow under each one. Every figure on the sheet is the same person: the same head size, the same garment and the same hand size; each pose takes the height its pose gives it, and a standing figure stands about three and a third heads tall. One thick warm dark-brown outline runs round the whole silhouette of each figure, and the head's outline is the one line inside it: none on the nose, the ear or the hairline, and the hair, the ear and the garments meet as flat colour, never as their own outlined pieces. The hair and the beard are one brown, yet never one shape: the hair is its own shape behind the head, the face and its beard one shape in front of it, and a narrow dark band, the deep shade of that brown, nearly as dark as the outline, runs between the beard and each lock of hair beside it, as the kept concepts paint it, so the beard never runs into the hair. The key light comes from the upper left on every figure, whichever way it faces, so its lit side is always on the left and its far side turns a deeper hue of its own colour toward violet, never grey and never black. Each turn is its own drawing, never a mirror of another. Each arm is in its sleeve to the wrist, and each hand is a plain round paper circle of the skin's colour at its sleeve's end: no thumb, no fingers. The sleeve runs from the shoulder to the hand wherever the hand is, hanging at rest along the side or raised with it; a hand never floats free beside the body. No skin shows below the neck except the hands: never a bare arm, a forearm or a bare shoulder. A walking figure glides: both soles flat on the ground line, the feet close together, the body leaning a little into the travel, the hem swung back, never a stride. No lettering anywhere: no labels, no names, no numbers, no arrows, no text, no grid, no boxes or frames round the figures.
